title: Explicit deployment and live-version proof
outcomes: A configured release closes only after the declared target reports the expected released commit/version and optional package hash, with resumable effect identity.

in: Explicit no-deployment policy or required target/package/deploy/readback profile; controlled command adapters; package hash and live target observations; frozen deployment authority and resume-only recovery; shared finish/readback gates
out: Selecting or configuring a real production provider
boundaries: Trusted canonical controller and explicit command adapter; configured target must provide authoritative operation/live-state observations

decision_rights: Authorize execution and choose model; GO on 2026-09-13
Implement bounded contract choices and document compatibility behavior

constraints: Deployment is a separate explicit run authorization, never inferred from model choice, Git push permission or an adopted profile. Freeze target, commands, recovery policy and authority for resume.
Profiles explicitly choose no deployment with a reason or a required target. Providers and credentials remain user/onboarding inputs; only local fixtures are configured in this task.

Only structured argv adapters are supported. Package output is confined to controller-owned operational storage and hashed; released commit/version and target are bound to every observation. Commands must preserve verified product content.

Package/deploy command success alone is insufficient. Require structured authoritative target readback for the exact commit/version, optional package hash and operation identity. Missing credentials, wrong target/version and unknown readback keep the task pending.

Persist intent before effects. Require adapter idempotency support with a stable task/run/commit/target key; reconcile accepted-but-not-live, absent and unknown separately. Never infer absence from transport errors or retry an unknown effect with a new identity.
Reuse the serial publication reservation, native process guard and budgets. Cleanup stays separate; no rollback or destructive recovery is inferred from ordinary release authority.
Use the strict completion gate and preserve historical release proof meaning. Explicit no-deployment and absent legacy deployment settings do not claim live service verification.
No GitHub Actions and no invented production destinations.

quality_attributes.scenario: Deploy exits zero but wrong commit/version is running
Deploy acknowledgement is lost or live propagation is delayed
quality_attributes.measure: Duplicate deployment effects with a new identity

quality_attributes.scenario: Target, credentials, recovery policy or deploy permission is absent
Legacy release-only history is read after deployment support lands
quality_attributes.measure: Fabricated live proof or broken historical reporting

risks: A command adapter is trusted infrastructure: it must query the target rather than echo requested values and must honor its idempotency contract.
External deployment and live health are separate observations; accepted or unknown operations must not be called complete.
